title: Custom platform with payment for work done

company.company_business: IT implementation and managed services for mid-size Indian businesses

narrative_template:
Kalmira is building a custom claims platform for {customer} on Kalmira's own development servers, to be handed over at the end. The design is so specific to the customer that it could not be sold to anyone else without major rework. If the customer cancels, the contract makes it pay for the work done to date plus a reasonable margin.

Is revenue recognised over time or at a point in time? If over time, which paragraph 35 criterion is met?

Round amounts to the nearest rupee and percentages to one decimal place. All names are fictional.

rubric.text: Over time under 35(c): no alternative use and an enforceable right to payment for work to date.

explanation: 35(c) needs both: the asset has no alternative use to the entity (para 36), and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date, including a reasonable margin (para 37).

mistakes.feedback: Handover at the end does not decide it. The platform has no alternative use (para 36) and the contract gives an enforceable right to payment for work to date (para 37), so 35(c) is met.
The platform sits on Kalmira's servers, so the customer does not control it while it is built and 35(b) fails. 35(c) is met instead.
The customer gets no benefit until the platform is handed over, so 35(a) fails. 35(c) is met: no alternative use and a right to payment for work to date.
